title: BAFTA 向英国和美国的 112 位受助者发放逾 27 万英镑，支持游戏、影视职业发展
content:
BAFTA awards over £270,000 to 112 recipients in UK and US to support career growth in games, film, and TV | GamesIndustry.biz

.
BAFTA has awarded over £270,000 in grants to 112 recipients in the UK and North America under its
2026 Prince William BAFTA Bursary
and scholarship programmes.
Both programmes support emerging creatives in games, film, and television by offering financial and practical assistance to help them build their careers.
The Prince William Bursary supported 100 recipients, representing a 40% increase from last year.
The bursary offers grants of up to £2,000 to individuals in Wales, Scotland, England, and Northern Ireland to cover essential costs such as training, equipment, software, relocation, and driving lessons.
BAFTA found that 98% of recipients from the 2024 and 2025 cohorts said the grants "enabled them to access career opportunities they otherwise could not have taken up," while 88.2% found that "receiving a BAFTA bursary significantly boosted their confidence in navigating the industry."
2026 UK Bursary games recipients include:
Bellayna Lopez – 2D game artist & animator
Erin Curtis – freelance 2D game artist
Jessica Murray – game designer and writer
Leviathan Vi Amare – technical artist
Sean Simmons – freelance illustrator and concept artist
Serina Lopez – 2D artist x game producer
Symoné – game designer
In the UK, scholarship recipients will receive up to £12,000 for tuition and living costs, in addition to mentoring and free access to BAFTA's year-round events.
In the
US
, recipients will receive up to $60,000 to support study at institutions such as Columbia University, Loyola Marymount University, New York University, School for Visual Arts, and Stanford University.
The UK scholarship program is supported by The Reuben Foundation and BAFTA patrons. The US program is supported by the Fulbright Program, Sir Mark Pigott KBE, and Tina Micklethwait.
2026 UK Scholars (games) include:
Hamzah Ali, Staffordshire University, Reuben Scholar, MA Games Art
Ava Rogerson, Norwich University of the Arts (NUA), BAFTA Scholarship, BA Games Art and Design
"BAFTA is passionate about the need to invest in fresh talent that the future of our industries relies on," said BAFTA deputy chair Hilary Rosen.
"The Prince William BAFTA Bursary and Scholarships programmes do exactly this – giving life-changing grants to emerging creatives who otherwise might well have been locked out of a career in the screen arts. We are delighted to announce the 2026 cohort and can't wait to see what they go on to achieve."
